We decided to purchase another KitchenAid dishwasher when our old one that was 12 years old finally gave up. There are some great features on the new machine but there are a couple of significant changes in the materials they used in the new machine compared to the old which don't work because they are now made of plastic rather than metal utilized on the old machine. First the postives: . 1) I love how quiet the new dishwasher is. The 39 dBA is practically silent which is important with an open kitchen/family room. We hear the occasional swish of water but it is much quieter than our old version partly due to improved insulation. You could see the increase in insulation and sound deadening materials during installation. 2) I also really like the redesigned utensil holder. The small holes that allow the utensils to be kept apart are a well designed upgrade to the new machine. I do wish they had made all the holes the same size as it is a constant game of “will it fit” since some holes are large and some are smaller. It would cause a lot less frustration when loading the utensils if they were all the same slze. 3) We had high hopes for the third rack. It is a fantastic additon to be able to wash lids and other FLAT items. In all honesty, with the 3rd rack we are still learning what items make it useful. The clearance is very low and even a large serving spoon or BBQ tongs don't fit well due to the low clearance and the curious multi level design of the rack. The rack seems to be designed with nubs for additional silverwear but I would rather have had space for serving utensils, long BBQ tongs and the like. Now for the negatives:. 1) On the old machine the adjustable legs for levelling the machine were metal and screwed into metal. They were strong and were up to the task and couldn't be damaged while levelling and raising the machine. On the new machine the mechanism for raising/ lowering and levelling the machine uses PLASTIC parts. The plastic parts support the entire weight of the dishwasher and take significant strain when levelling the machine. The plastic threads on the plastic screws were not strong enough to support the forces applied while levelling the machine and SHEARED OFF the plastic threads, thereby leaving the adjustable legs no longer adjustable, and the mechanism to level the dishwasher no longer functional. I was forced to use shims to level the machine. I'm really disappointed that such an important part has been replaced by cheap plastic. 2) Similarly, the kick plate also incorporates plastic (previously metal on the old machine) and the thick metal screws that hold the kick plate in place are screwed into plastic. This plastic is not up to the task and is too soft and after removing the kickplate once or twice the screwholes are now unable to secure the kickplate and the screws just fall out. This is despite the fact that I hand tightened these screws with a screwdriver and was exceptionally gentle and cautious as I knew it was screwed into plastic. The attempt by the manufacturer to save money by replacing important parts with plastic has resulted in my dissatisfaction with these key parts of the dishwasher and tainted my overall impression of my new KitchenAid dishwasher. I will be very cautious before I purchase a third KitchenAid dishwasher after being a loyal and satisfied customer all these years.

The way to distinguish the latest models is to check whether or not there is an E at the end. We could have gone with a built-in dishwasher, but we didn't really need one because we were going to put the dishwasher in the corner. But in the case of a freestanding dishwasher, if you just take off the lid and store it, you can take it with you when you move, and it can be installed right away. The lid is still in storage, and the LG technician put it back in nicely, and he also organized the remaining space nicely. Comments (English): [ Aunt, I should have brought it in earlier. ] || ---------------- || I like to wash dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed me to buy it. Looking back, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to buy the latest dishwasher with TrueSteam, TrueDry, and Hot Air Dry, and it even comes with a 10% energy rebate. I really had a lot of concerns, including LG or Samsung, 12-seater or 14-seater, built-in or freestanding, whether it should have lighting or not, whether to include glide rails, and whether to have a frying pan holder or not. In the end, I decided to buy a freestanding 14-seater with a frying pan holder that has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to distinguish the latest models is to check whether or not there is an E at the end. We could have gone with a built-in dishwasher, but we didn't really need one because we were going to put the dishwasher in the corner. If we did, there would be issues with the size of the house we're moving to, and if we did, we'd have to take it with us. So, we often end up leaving it behind. But in the case of a freestanding dishwasher, if you just take off the lid and store it, you can take it with you when you move, and it can be installed right away. The lid is still in storage, and the LG technician put it back in nicely, and he also organized the remaining space nicely. The lower cabinet under the corner sink is unusable, but it was something we considered when we brought the dishwasher in, and we ended up paying the extra cost. I've been using it for a week, and it's much fluffier than I thought, which is nice. Of course, there is some larvae, but since the internal circulation dries the dishes as soon as the automatic door opens, this alone dries them well. The owner said that it would be good to leave the door open a little longer after the automatic door opens. I am using solid detergent, and it washes cleanly even with only half the amount. However, the disappointing thing is that the steamed eggs in the stand container do not wash well. You have to wash those by hand. If this part is perfect, it would be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rail, but I have not used the glide rail, but it is smooth enough. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. Tetris requires more practice than I thought, so it seems like it will take some getting used to, but I am getting used to it little by little. Unfortunately, the soap door dispenser has had persistent issues with it becoming uncoupled. We repeated the process to have a repair completed hoping they would exchange the components, but they found the same issue. The solenoid was uncoupled and they just snapped it back into place. After the warranty expired, I (an engineer by trade) wired the solenoid so that it couldn't come uncoupled, and so far it's been working correctly. However, most recently, it's been stopping mid cycle and flashing an error code, which just says to disconnect the power supply, then reconnect. KitchenAid won't help with troubleshooting, and only offers to send a repair technician for $380.I don't think a new appliance should have this many issues in such a short time, so I'm very disappointed with what I'm left with, and not confident that it will be dependable for years of even light service. On another note, when it is running correctly, it does a great job. It's very quiet, completes a normal cycle in roughly 2 hours, and dries well when using rinse aid.

Delivery and installation (including uninstalling old machine, taking it out and unpacking and installing the machine, "upgrading" electrical and plumbing took FORTY (40) MINUTES. For this Best Buy charged me $249.99 installation (plus an installation kit for $37.99) plus 49.99 for Haul away plus $39.99 for delivery. Then add $400 for the "upgrades" (perhaps 15 minutes work plus parts were needed--but that bill was NOT itemized). So a $649.99 machine had a total cost of $1473.45 including tax. Best Buy should be ashamed of themselves charging $290 for delivery and installation and letting the installer charge an additional $400 on top of that. They DID warn me there could be an additional cost; they said they didn't know how much. Given I paid them $250 for installation they needed to limit the rest--$400 for very little work. I estimate the parts were under $100 (from the Home Depot site). Summary: Best Buy is not a "best buy"; they were a party to the consumer paying more for installation than the cost of the machine. To add insult to injury it took Best Buy about two weeks to install--only after I was not happy about three weeks

My excellent 24 year old dishwasher finally sprung a leak, so it was time. I ordered this Bosch. I got it set up and I like the wifi connection. I find it useful. The dishwasher does a good job and is quiet. Unfortunately, recently when I was washing the front of the dishwasher, I discovered a crack in the front of the machine, the plastic covering the handle. Sentence (English): We bought it this dishwasher as a replacement for another brand dishwasher that started leaking and had to be replaced.
Comments (English): [ 18" Haier Dishwasher Installation ] || ---------------- || We bought it this dishwasher as a replacement for another brand dishwasher that started leaking and had to be replaced. We hoped that this dishwasher would be easy to install, like being just plug and play, as all the plumbing and electric outlets were already in place from the previous dishwasher installation. However, it turned out that there is no electric power cord attached to the dishwasher that can be plugged into the wall outlet to begin with. Nor was the power cord to be installed included in the package along with a plastic rubber piece needed to hold the power cord in place. The dishwasher needed to be opened up and a power cord bought separately and installed in place. In addition, for the plumbing outlet, an elbow joint required for installation was missing and had to be bought separately and installed inside the dishwasher with a lot of difficulty. I think this is the result of the manufacturer wanting to make the dishwasher compatible with the plumbing and electric system of different countries, but at much extra cost and effort on the part of end consumer. In the end, we ended up paying $300 on top of the purchase price for a technician to come and install the dishwasher, which otherwise should have cost of nothing if the dishwasher manufacturer specifically included all the installation parts themselves and packaged it installation-ready from the factory.

Sentence (English): I like to wash dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed me to buy it.
Comments (English): [ Aunt, I should have brought it in earlier. ] || ---------------- || I like to wash dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed me to buy it. Looking back, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to buy the latest dishwasher with TrueSteam, TrueDry, and Hot Air Dry, and it even comes with a 10% energy rebate. I really had a lot of concerns, including LG or Samsung, 12-seater or 14-seater, built-in or freestanding, whether it should have lighting or not, whether to include glide rails, and whether to have a frying pan holder or not. In the end, I decided to buy a freestanding 14-seater with a frying pan holder that has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to distinguish the latest models is to check whether or not there is an E at the end. We could have gone with a built-in dishwasher, but we didn't really need one because we were going to put the dishwasher in the corner. If we did, there would be issues with the size of the house we're moving to, and if we did, we'd have to take it with us. So, we often end up leaving it behind. But in the case of a freestanding dishwasher, if you just take off the lid and store it, you can take it with you when you move, and it can be installed right away. The lid is still in storage, and the LG technician put it back in nicely, and he also organized the remaining space nicely. The lower cabinet under the corner sink is unusable, but it was something we considered when we brought the dishwasher in, and we ended up paying the extra cost. I've been using it for a week, and it's much fluffier than I thought, which is nice. Of course, there is some larvae, but since the dishes are dried by internal circulation as soon as the automatic door opens, this alone dries them. The owner said that it would be good to leave the door open a little longer after the automatic door opens. I am using solid detergent, and it washes cleanly even with only half the amount. However, the disappointing thing is that the steamed eggs in the stand container do not wash off. You have to wash those by hand. If this part is perfect, it would be the best. And what I was worried about was the glide rail, but I haven't used the glide rail, but it is smooth enough. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. Tetris requires more practice than I thought, so I think it will take some getting used to, but I am getting used to it little by little. - I'm adding a review from two weeks ago. It's really nice that the frying pan holder can hold a frying pan. If you put a frying pan with a peeling coating in it, the peeled part will expand when it meets the hot air, which will make it worse. It was a frying pan that I bought not long ago, so it was my fault for not checking it thoroughly before putting it in. I also changed the frying pan while I was at it. There are frying pans that are dishwasher safe, and you have to be careful because the coating can peel off. You have to check it carefully before using it. And I keep it on auto mode, and I don't use the hot air mode because the auto drying mode dries well enough. When the dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-dry them and put them in the dishwasher, and when the dishes come out in the evening, I run them all at once. The download course can now store three courses, so I added the upper rapid mode and use the downloaded course when there are only a few courses left. The upper rapid mode finishes in about 30 minutes if no additional functions (hot air, sterilization, rinsing, etc.) are used. It's a highly satisfactory product in many ways. This model has an optional light, which is useful at night, but considering it turns off automatically while I'm playing dishwasher Tetris, I don't think it would be too inconvenient without it. In the end, I decided to buy a freestanding 14-seater with a frying pan holder that has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to distinguish the latest models is to check whether or not there is an E at the end. We could have gone with a built-in dishwasher, but we didn't really need one because we were going to put the dishwasher in the corner. If we did, there would be issues with the size of the house we're moving to, and if we did, we'd have to take it with us. So, we often end up leaving it behind. But in the case of a freestanding dishwasher, if you just take off the lid and store it, you can take it with you when you move, and it can be installed right away. The lid is still in storage, and the LG technician put it back in nicely, and he also organized the remaining space nicely. The lower cabinet under the corner sink is unusable, but it was something we considered when we brought the dishwasher in, and we ended up paying the extra cost. I've been using it for a week, and it's much fluffier than I thought, which is nice. Of course, there is some larvae, but since the dishes are dried by internal circulation as soon as the automatic door opens, this alone dries them. The owner said that it would be good to leave the door open a little longer after the automatic door opens. I am using solid detergent, and it washes cleanly even with only half the amount. However, the disappointing thing is that the steamed eggs in the stand container do not wash off. You have to wash those by hand. If this part is perfect, it would be the best. And what I was worried about was the glide rail, but I haven't used the glide rail, but it is smooth enough. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. Tetris requires more practice than I thought, so I think it will take some getting used to, but I am getting used to it little by little. - I'm adding a review from two weeks ago. It's really nice that the frying pan holder can hold a frying pan. If you put a frying pan with a peeling coating in it, the peeled part will expand when it meets the hot air, which will make it worse. It was a frying pan that I bought not long ago, so it was my fault for not checking it thoroughly before putting it in. I also changed the frying pan while I was at it. There are frying pans that are dishwasher safe, and you have to be careful because the coating can peel off. You have to check it carefully before using it. And I keep it on auto mode, and I don't use the hot air mode because the auto drying mode dries well enough. When the dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-dry them and put them in the dishwasher, and when the dishes come out in the evening, I run them all at once. The download course can now store three courses, so I added the upper rapid mode and use the downloaded course when there are only a few courses left. The upper rapid mode finishes in about 30 minutes if no additional functions (hot air, sterilization, rinsing, etc.) are used. It's a highly satisfactory product in many ways. This model has an optional light, which is useful at night, but considering it turns off automatically while I'm playing dishwasher Tetris, I don't think it would be too inconvenient without it. I guess the light is just for a bit of coolness? I hope you choose the dishwasher option that suits your situation~~ :) If you agree with my review of my own purchase, please give it a quick vote~~ :)

In the end, I decided to buy a freestanding 14-seater with a frying pan holder that has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to distinguish the latest models is to check whether or not there is an E at the end. We could have gone with a built-in dishwasher, but we didn't really need one because we were going to put the dishwasher in the corner. If we did, there would be issues with the size of the house we're moving to, and if we did, we'd have to take it with us. So, we often end up leaving it behind. But in the case of a freestanding dishwasher, if you just take off the lid and store it, you can take it with you when you move, and it can be installed right away. The lid is still in storage, and the LG technician put it back in nicely, and he also organized the remaining space nicely. The lower cabinet under the corner sink is unusable, but it was something we considered when we brought the dishwasher in, and we ended up paying the extra cost. I've been using it for a week, and it's much fluffier than I thought, which is nice. Of course, there is some larvae, but since the dishes are dried by internal circulation as soon as the automatic door opens, this alone dries them. The owner said that it would be good to leave the door open a little longer after the automatic door opens. I am using solid detergent, and it washes cleanly even with only half the amount. However, the disappointing thing is that the steamed eggs in the stand container do not wash off. You have to wash those by hand. If this part is perfect, it would be the best. And what I was worried about was the glide rail, but I haven't used the glide rail, but it is smooth enough. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. Tetris requires more practice than I thought, so I think it will take some getting used to, but I am getting used to it little by little. - I'm adding a review from two weeks ago. It's really nice that the frying pan holder can hold a frying pan. If you put a frying pan with a peeling coating in it, the peeled part will expand when it meets the hot air, which will make it worse. It was a frying pan that I bought not long ago, so it was my fault for not checking it thoroughly before putting it in. I also changed the frying pan while I was at it. There are frying pans that are dishwasher safe, and you have to be careful because the coating can peel off. You have to check it carefully before using it. And I keep it on auto mode, and I don't use the hot air mode because the auto drying mode dries well enough. When the dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-dry them and put them in the dishwasher, and when the dishes come out in the evening, I run them all at once. The download course can now store three courses, so I added the upper rapid mode and use the downloaded course when there are only a few courses left. The upper rapid mode finishes in about 30 minutes if no additional functions (hot air, sterilization, rinsing, etc.) are used. It's a highly satisfactory product in many ways. This model has an optional light, which is useful at night, but considering it turns off automatically while I'm playing dishwasher Tetris, I don't think it would be too inconvenient without it. I guess the light is just for a bit of coolness? I've been using it for a week, and it's much fluffier than I thought, which is nice. Of course, there is some larvae, but since the dishes are dried by internal circulation as soon as the automatic door opens, this alone dries them. The owner said that it would be good to leave the door open a little longer after the automatic door opens. I am using solid detergent, and it washes cleanly even with only half the amount. However, the disappointing thing is that the steamed eggs in the stand container do not wash off. You have to wash those by hand. If this part is perfect, it would be the best. And what I was worried about was the glide rail, but I haven't used the glide rail, but it is smooth enough. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. There are frying pans that are dishwasher safe, and you have to be careful because the coating can peel off. You have to check it carefully before using it. And I keep it on auto mode, and I don't use the hot air mode because the auto drying mode dries well enough. When the dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-dry them and put them in the dishwasher, and when the dishes come out in the evening, I run them all at once. The download course can now store three courses, so I added the upper rapid mode and use the downloaded course when there are only a few courses left. The upper rapid mode finishes in about 30 minutes if no additional functions (hot air, sterilization, rinsing, etc.) are used. It's a highly satisfactory product in many ways. This model has an optional light, which is useful at night, but considering it turns off automatically while I'm playing dishwasher Tetris, I don't think it would be too inconvenient without it. I guess the light is just for a bit of coolness? But in the case of a freestanding dishwasher, if you just take off the lid and store it, you can take it with you when you move, and it can be installed right away. The lower cabinet under the corner sink is unusable, but it was something we considered when we brought the dishwasher in, and we ended up paying the extra cost. I've been using it for a week, and it's much fluffier than I thought, which is nice. Of course, there is some larvae, but since the dishes are dried by internal circulation as soon as the automatic door opens, this alone dries them. The owner said that it would be good to leave the door open a little longer after the automatic door opens. I am using solid detergent, and it washes cleanly even with only half the amount. However, the disappointing thing is that the steamed eggs in the stand container do not wash off. You have to wash those by hand. If this part is perfect, it would be the best. And what I was worried about was the glide rail, but I haven't used the glide rail, but it is smooth enough. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. And I keep it on auto mode, and I don't use the hot air mode because the auto drying mode dries well enough. When the dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-dry them and put them in the dishwasher, and when the dishes come out in the evening, I run them all at once. I guess the light is just for a bit of coolness? Comments (English): [ Aunt, I should have brought it in earlier. ] || ---------------- || I like to wash dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed me to buy it. I really had a lot of concerns, including LG or Samsung, 12-seater or 14-seater, built-in or freestanding, whether it should have lighting or not, whether to include glide rails, and whether to have a frying pan holder or not. In the end, I decided to buy a freestanding 14-seater with a frying pan holder that has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to distinguish the latest models is to check whether or not there is an E at the end. We could have gone with a built-in dishwasher, but we didn't really need one because we were going to put the dishwasher in the corner. If we did, there would be issues with the size of the house we're moving to, and if we did, we'd have to take it with us. So, we often end up leaving it behind. But in the case of a freestanding dishwasher, if you just take off the lid and store it, you can take it with you when you move, and it can be installed right away. The lid is still in storage, and the LG technician put it back in nicely, and he also organized the remaining space nicely. The lower cabinet under the corner sink is unusable, but it was something we considered when we brought the dishwasher in, and we ended up paying the extra cost. I've been using it for a week, and it's much fluffier than I thought, which is nice. Of course, there is some larvae, but since the dishes are dried by internal circulation as soon as the automatic door opens, this alone dries them. The owner said that it would be good to leave the door open a little longer after the automatic door opens. I am using solid detergent, and it washes cleanly even with only half the amount. However, the disappointing thing is that the steamed eggs in the stand container do not wash off. You have to wash those by hand. If this part is perfect, it would be the best. And what I was worried about was the glide rail, but I haven't used the glide rail, but it is smooth enough. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. Tetris requires more practice than I thought, so I think it will take some getting used to, but I am getting used to it little by little. - I'm adding a review from two weeks ago. It's really nice that the frying pan holder can hold a frying pan. If you put a frying pan with a peeling coating in it, the peeled part will expand when it meets the hot air, which will make it worse. It was a frying pan that I bought not long ago, so it was my fault for not checking it thoroughly before putting it in. I also changed the frying pan while I was at it. There are frying pans that are dishwasher safe, and you have to be careful because the coating can peel off. You have to check it carefully before using it. And I keep it on auto mode, and I don't use the hot air mode because the auto drying mode dries well enough. When the dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-dry them and put them in the dishwasher, and when the dishes come out in the evening, I run them all at once. The download course can now store three courses, so I added the upper rapid mode and use the downloaded course when there are only a few courses left. The upper rapid mode finishes in about 30 minutes if no additional functions (hot air, sterilization, rinsing, etc.) are used. It's a highly satisfactory product in many ways. This model has an optional light, which is useful at night, but considering it turns off automatically while I'm playing dishwasher Tetris, I don't think it would be too inconvenient without it. I guess the light is just for a bit of coolness? I hope you choose the dishwasher option that suits your situation~~ :) If you agree with my review of my own purchase, please give it a quick vote~~ :)

The way to distinguish the latest models is to check whether or not there is an E at the end. We could have gone with a built-in dishwasher, but we didn't really need one because we were going to put the dishwasher in the corner. But in the case of a freestanding dishwasher, if you just take off the lid and store it, you can take it with you when you move, and it can be installed right away. The lower cabinet under the corner sink is unusable, but it was something we considered when we brought the dishwasher in, and we ended up paying the extra cost. I've been using it for a week, and it's much fluffier than I thought, which is nice. Of course, there is some larvae, but since the dishes are dried by internal circulation as soon as the automatic door opens, this alone dries them. The owner said that it would be good to leave the door open a little longer after the automatic door opens. I am using solid detergent, and it washes cleanly even with only half the amount. However, the disappointing thing is that the steamed eggs in the stand container do not wash off. You have to wash those by hand. If this part is perfect, it would be the best. And what I was worried about was the glide rail, but I haven't used the glide rail, but it is smooth enough. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. There are frying pans that are dishwasher safe, and you have to be careful because the coating can peel off. You have to check it carefully before using it. And I keep it on auto mode, and I don't use the hot air mode because the auto drying mode dries well enough. When the dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-dry them and put them in the dishwasher, and when the dishes come out in the evening, I run them all at once. The download course can now store three courses, so I added the upper rapid mode and use the downloaded course when there are only a few courses left. There are frying pans that are dishwasher safe, and you have to be careful because the coating can peel off. You have to check it carefully before using it. And I keep it on auto mode, and I don't use the hot air mode because the auto drying mode dries well enough. When the dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-dry them and put them in the dishwasher, and when the dishes come out in the evening, I run them all at once. Sentence (English): I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one.
Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Sentence (English): I really agonized over the decision.
Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Sentence (English): 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting.
Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Sentence (English): Built-in vs. freestanding.
Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Sentence (English): Should I include Glide Rails or not?
Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Sentence (English): After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting.
Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)
