Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Comments (English): [ I should have brought Auntie in sooner. ] || ---------------- || I prefer washing dishes by hand, so I tried to put off buying a dishwasher as much as possible, but my husband pushed for it, so I ended up buying one. Now that I have it, I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner, but thanks to him, I was able to purchase the latest model that features True Steam, True Drying, and Hot Air Drying, plus I can get a 10% energy rebate. I really agonized over the decision. LG vs. Samsung. 12-place setting vs. 14-place setting. Built-in vs. freestanding. Then, should I have lighting or not? Should I include Glide Rails or not? Should I have a frying pan rack or not? After much deliberation, I finally decided on a freestanding 14-place setting model with a frying pan rack that also has lighting. This model is the DFE6HBGE. The way to identify the latest models is to check whether or not an 'E' is attached at the very end. We could have gotten a built-in model, but since we plan to place it in the corner, we realized it wasn't strictly necessary. With built-in models, if we move later, there can be issues with removing parts or size compatibility with the new home, so people often leave them behind. However, with a freestanding model, I was told that as long as you remove and store the lid, you can take it with you immediately if you move, and installation is possible right away. The lid is currently in storage, and the LG technician put it away nicely. They also built a beautiful cabinet for the remaining space next to it. The lower cabinet in the corner sink area is no longer usable, but this was something we anticipated when getting the dishwasher, and we paid the additional cost. I've been using it for a week now, and I'm happy because the dishes come out much fresher and fluffier than I expected. Of course, I do a little pre-drying, but since the internal circulation dries as soon as the automatic door opens, that alone is enough to dry the dishes. The technician mentioned that it's good to leave the door open just a little bit after it opens automatically. I am currently using solid detergent. It washes thoroughly even if you only fill it halfway. However, the only downside is that steamed eggs cooked in stainless steel containers don't wash out; you have to hand-wash those. If that part could be done perfectly as well, it would truly be the best. Also, I was concerned about the glide rails; although I haven't used them yet, they are quite smooth. Other than that, I am mostly satisfied. The Tetris game requires more maneuvering than I expected, so I think I'll need some time to adapt, but I am gradually getting used to it. - Adding a review after 2 weeks. The frying pan holder is great because you can put frying pans in it. However, if you put in a frying pan with a worn coating, the peeled area expands upon contact with the hot air, causing the pan to deteriorate. It was a frying pan I hadn't had for long, so it was my fault for putting it in without checking enough. I ended up replacing the frying pan as well. There are frying pans that are dishwasher-safe, but you need to be careful with coated products, as the coating can actually peel off. You need to check carefully before using it. I've been running it on automatic mode continuously, and since the automatic drying setting dries well enough, I don't really bother using the hot air mode. If dishes pile up in the morning, I pre-wash them a bit before putting them in the dishwasher, and then run them all together when the evening wash comes out. Since you can now save three download cycles, I added the Top Rapid mode. I use a downloaded cycle for small loads, and the Top Rapid mode finishes the job in about 30 minutes if I don't use any extra functions (hot air, sanitizing, rinsing, etc.). It is a product I am very satisfied with in many ways. Oh, this model comes with an optional light. It is somewhat useful at night, but seeing as it automatically turns off while I'm playing Tetris with the dishwasher, I don't think it would be a huge inconvenience without the light. Is the light just for a bit of style? I hope you choose the dishwasher options that best suit your situation. :) If you agree with this review of a product I bought with my own money, please give it a thumbs up! :)

Sentence (English): I'm writing this review after 15 months of use, and we're fairly disappointed in it's build quality, and wish we had gone with something else.
Comments (English): [ Great When it's Functioning ] || ---------------- || I'm writing this review after 15 months of use, and we're fairly disappointed in it's build quality, and wish we had gone with something else. After installation, the dishwasher only ran for a few days, before the soap door dispenser stopped opening. We called for a warranty claim, which was a fairly easy process, but then had to wait two weeks for the repair. The solenoid on the door mechanism wasn't attached correctly from the factory. The technician snapped it into place, and all was well. We considered this annoying, but hopefully an honest mistake in assembly. Unfortunately, the soap door dispenser has had persistent issues with it becoming uncoupled. We repeated the process to have a repair completed hoping they would exchange the components, but they found the same issue. The solenoid was uncoupled and they just snapped it back into place. After the warranty expired, I (an engineer by trade) wired the solenoid so that it couldn't come uncoupled, and so far it's been working correctly. However, most recently, it's been stopping mid cycle and flashing an error code, which just says to disconnect the power supply, then reconnect. KitchenAid won't help with troubleshooting, and only offers to send a repair technician for $380. I don't think a new appliance should have this many issues in such a short time, so I'm very disappointed with what I'm left with, and not confident that it will be dependable for years of even light service. On another note, when it is running correctly, it does a great job. It's very quiet, completes a normal cycle in roughly 2 hours, and dries well when using rinse aid.

Sentence (English): This cleans the dishes fine, but has two major problems.
Comments (English): [ Doesn't dry dishes ] || ---------------- || This cleans the dishes fine, but has two major problems. Problem 1: Anything made out of plastic comes out dripping wet, even if you have extended or heated dry turned on . this is AFTER the inconceivably long 4 1/2 hour cycle. The drying problem is so bad that after we run it, we have to move the dishes to a drying rack on the counter for a full day before they're actually dry. Want to dry them by just popping the door after the cycle? Be prepared to wait two or three days. Problem 2: One of the spray arms is designed in such a way that it sprays against the door for part of its rotation. When that arm is running, there is a fairly loud and repeating sound of a jet of water hitting the door.This holds a ton of dishes compared to our old machine (a 14 year old bottom of the barrel plastic tub GE), but in every other way the GE was equal to or SO much better than this thing (namely, it got the dishes actually dry and had a nicer soap dispenser). If I could take it back, I would.One more note -- I mounted ours a bit proud of the edge of the counter so I can see the remaining cycle time while it's running (the display DOES stay on). I don't know who thought it was a good idea to put the controls in a spot where you can't see or access them while it's closed if it's mounted flush, but I wouldn't buy another top-control dishwasher . that one's on me, though, not Whirlpool. I should have known better.

Comments (English): [ BOSCH Small Dishwasher Review ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher is truly fantastic. It's narrow, feels small, but is truly spacious. Thanks to the additional cutlery drawer, the baskets really hold a lot. Various configurations are possible: foldable combs and adjustable basket height make it easy to fit even large pots. It has a convenient, backlit display that shows, among other things, the remaining cycle time. A 10-year warranty on the interior (stainless steel) and a flood-proof system guarantee safe, long-lasting operation. For those who love modern technology and remote control, there's an app that makes this possible. Możliwe są różne konfiguracje: składane grzebienie i regulowana wysokośc kosza sprawiają, że mozna tam włożyc nawet duże garnki :) 6 programów do wyboru, duzo dodtkowych funkcji ( np. skracanie czasu pracy, tryb cichy, czy dodatkowe suszenie, i inne :)) ma wygodny, podświetlany wyświetlacz, na którym m.in. widać czas do końca cyklu. 10 letnia gwaracja na wnetrze ( nierdzewka), oraz zawód przeciwzalaniowy gwaratuje bezpieczna dlugoletnią prace.  Dla miłośników nowoczesnych technolgii i zdalnego sterowania, mozna korzystac z aplikacji dzieki której jest to możliwe.Jesli chodzi o efekt wizualny: jest estetyczna, zgrabna, ładny srebrny szczotkowany kolor idealnie pasuje do moich pozostałych sprzetów. Nic dodać nic ująć :)

Sentence (English): Great quite
Product Overview: This dishwasher was installed at my parents' house as a Chuseok gift.
Comments (English): [ No need for expensive brands! Hot air drying + 3-stage washing for great value. ] || ---------------- || Product Overview: This dishwasher was installed at my parents' house as a Chuseok gift. To ensure a thorough review, I've used it for about a month. We currently have a Samsung 6-seater countertop dishwasher, but honestly, the cleaning power is virtually the same. In fact, the Midea dishwasher has a hot air drying function, which leaves dishes crisper after drying. It's a product with excellent functionality and quality, worthy of its price tag. It comes in a variety of colors, and the pastel shades are incredibly pretty. --- Delivery & Installation: After ordering with Rocket Installation, I made a reservation for a preferred date and had it installed right away after a Happy Call! The technician even provided helpful instructions, making it easy for seniors to use. Its slim size takes up little space in the kitchen and fits neatly. While it's a bit narrow, the two-tier basket holds plenty of dishes. The water supply requires a hole, but it's only about 1cm deep, so it's not noticeable. --- Cleaning Power & Function: The cleaning power is comparable to that of the Samsung product. It cleans dishes sparklingly, leaving no stubborn stains on the surface. The three-stage rotating blades ensure water reaches every nook and cranny, ensuring thorough cleaning even with a two-tier basket. Samsung countertops feature two-tier blades, one above the other. This two-tier basket design offers excellent space utilization. Samsung countertops typically only have one tier, so they don't hold as many dishes as you might think. This product efficiently accommodates everything from small cups to large bowls. The hot air drying function ensures virtually no moisture even after washing, and even plastic items dry much more fluffily. The automatic door-opening feature eliminates internal moisture and odors. All you need to do is occasionally clean the filter and interior. I always thoroughly clean the larvae even when using a dishwasher because it keeps the filter clean. If you don't remove debris, you'll need to clean the filter regularly, which can be a hassle. The baskets are also completely removable for easy cleaning, and the two-tier basket can be removed for larger pots. --- Noise & Efficiency: The noise level during operation is comparable to that of a weak electric fan, making it comfortable to use even at night. My parents were very pleased with the unit, as it uses less water and doesn't break the electricity bill. It may look small, but for a family of two, it can handle six people, so if there aren't many dishes, it can't be fully loaded, so two loads are used. --- Disappointing Points: 1. This unit doesn't have a separate detergent dispenser, so you probably won't need to use a separate rinse aid. However, you don't have to! You can just dump detergent into the dishwasher or place it in the groove on the door, and it will roll away. 2. Since the interior is designed for six people, it's best to separate large pots. --- Overall Review: Design, Cleaning Power, Drying Power, Noise, Value for Money. Its cleaning power rivals that of Samsung, and with the addition of hot air drying, three-stage wing cleaning, and two-stage baskets, its practicality is even greater. My parents, who weren't sure about dishwashers, were surprised by the squeaky-clean dishes and the hot air drying that left them piping hot. The rocket-mounted design and slim size make it a perfect space-saver. It's a perfect value for money item. After submitting my original review (below) on Oct 3, 2025, Whirlpool contacted me and agreed to replace the dishwasher with any similarly priced Whirlpool product. I accepted the offer and the installer just left the house - new KitchenAid installed, old Maytag gone. The installer was from an independent appliance dealer and after seeing the original installation from when the house was built, he said that with the way the drain hose had been routed, any machine would have a tough time surviving for very long. He drilled new holes in the back of the cabinets and rerouted the drain hose from the machine to the disposal. A couple of points to consider: 1) original KitchenAid dishwasher that was installed when we built the house never had any problem with the pump and always finished its cycle with the old drain hose routing, so not sure what was different about the Maytag unit that kept failing. Maytag's service contractor was here twice and never mentioned anything about the drain hose routing - even replaced the drain hose once without changing its routing. So not sure where real problem lies - Maytag unit or original installer (or both), but kudos to Whirlpool for trying to make it right. Just hoping the new machine gives me years of trouble-free service. Original review:. Purchased this in July 2024. By January 2025, the dishwasher would not pump out the water and could not finish the cycle. Would wake up to error code. Maytag arranged for repair from local appliance service company, and they replaced the drain pump and drain hose. Worked fine for a while, but same problem and error code started again at the one year mark. Since I was a couple of weeks beyond the 1-year warranty date, Maytag wanted me to purchase repair plan, which would cost more annually than I paid for the dishwasher, but then agreed to go ahead and try to repair again under warranty. Service tech replaced the pump again, and also replaced the control board. One week later, the error code showed up again and I woke up to an unfinished cycle. I regret purchasing this machine and will start looking for a different brand. I will try to get refund from Maytag, but am not optimistic.

We ended up calling a plumber and they were able to install and haul away the old unit. In the end I kind of preferred this because they had to install a new hose and shut off switch that was compatible with the dishwasher. It took three plumbers in 2 days to realize they needed to tilt the machine so they could really turn the piece to tighten it fully. No more leaks after that. However I feel if home depot installed it and that happened it would have taken way more time to get someone out here to look at it.I am including a picture of the silver connector stop valve that you need or home depot cannot install it. If you don't have it then I would suggest paying for the install kit and hiring a plumber as the delivery guys cannot do this work and you will have to reschedule your delivery.

Sentence (English): Maximum satisfaction with Bosch SMH4EVX08E I purchased the Bosch SMH4EVX08E dishwasher on 19.10.2025 and I am very satisfied with it.
Comments (English): [ My first BOSCH dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Maximum satisfaction with Bosch SMH4EVX08E I purchased the Bosch SMH4EVX08E dishwasher on 19.10.2025 and I am very satisfied with it. It washes perfectly, the dishes are beautifully clean and dry after each cycle, even plastic bowls. I like the quiet operation - you can hardly hear it, which I especially appreciate in the evening. The third drawer for cutlery and the option to connect via the Home Connect application, where I can monitor the program progress and consumption, are very practical. The programs are clear, easy to use and the design looks elegant. I also appreciate the option to shorten the cycle via SpeedPerfect and the ecological program that saves water and electricity. Overall, I rate this dishwasher as a reliable, high-quality and quiet appliance with a good price-performance ratio. I would definitely buy it again.
Comments (Original): [ Moja prvá myčka BOSCH ] || ---------------- || Maximálna spokojnosť s Bosch SMH4EVX08EUmývačku Bosch SMH4EVX08E som zakúpila 19.10.2025 a som s ňou veľmi spokojná. Umýva perfektne, riady sú po každom cykle krásne čisté a suché, aj plastové misky. Páči sa mi tichý chod – takmer ju nepočuť, čo oceňujem hlavne večer. Veľmi praktická je tretia zásuvka na príbory a možnosť pripojenia cez aplikáciu Home Connect, kde viem sledovať priebeh programu a spotrebu.Programy sú prehľadné, ovládanie jednoduché a dizajn pôsobí elegantne. Oceňujem aj možnosť skrátenia cyklu cez SpeedPerfect a ekologický program, ktorý šetrí vodu aj elektrinu.Celkovo hodnotím túto umývačku ako spoľahlivý, kvalitný a tichý spotrebič s dobrým pomerom ceny a výkonu. Určite by som ju kúpila znova.

Sentence (English): This is my second Bosch dishwasher, and once again, I'm very happy with my choice.
Comments (English): [ reliable ] || ---------------- || This is my second Bosch dishwasher, and once again, I'm very happy with my choice. The previous model served me well for many years – it always cleaned dishes thoroughly and never caused any problems. The new model maintains the same high level of quality and is also remarkably quiet during operation, which makes a real difference – you can barely hear it running (which is important when the kitchen is connected to the living room). Dishes are perfectly clean after every cycle, the programs are clear, and the operation is very intuitive. The only drawback I noticed is the lack of automatic door opening after the program ends – this would have been convenient, especially when drying. Apart from this minor drawback, I highly recommend it; it's a solid machine at a reasonable price that meets all expectations.
Comments (Original): [ niezawodna ] || ---------------- || To już moja druga zmywarka marki Bosch i ponownie jestem bardzo zadowolona z wyboru. Porzedni model służył mi przez wiele lat - zawsze dokładnie domywał naczynia, nigdy nie sprawiał żadnych problemów. Nowy model utrzymuje ten sam, wysoki poziom jakości a dodatkowo jest niezwykłe cichy podaczas pracy, co naprawdę robi różnicę - praktycznie nie słychać , że pacuje (co jest ważne kiedy kuchnia jest połączona z salonem). Naczynia po każdym cyklu są idealnie czyste, programy są czytelne a obsługa bardzo intuicyjna.Jedyny minus jaki zauważyłam, to brak automatycznego otwierania drzwiczek po zakończoniu programu - byłoby to wygodne rozwiązanie, szczególnie przy suszeniu.Poza tym drobnym mankamentem, zdecydowanie polecam, solidny sprzęt w rozsądnej cenie, który spełnia wszystkie oczekiwania.

Comments (English): [ Wanted to love it. Did not. ] || ---------------- || First of all, every negative thing you read in these reviews is true. If you're like me, you read reviews before making a major purchase, and, in the nicest way possible, some of the reviewers are a little hyperbolic, so you take it all with a grain of salt. We purchased a competitor's product and it died after 5 years which was super disappointing. At the time we were debating between a Bosch (which everyone seems to love) and the competitor, which is known for appliances that are cool but sometimes don't last. So when the competitor's dishwasher broke, we weren't surprised, and decided to bite the bullet and get the premium brand we probably should have got in the first place. Now here I am a few weeks later doing something I never expected- returning a major appliance because I hate it, and writing a review to save others the hassle. It smells bad inside. The dishes don't get dry. You can't set the delay without using the app. But the racks… the racks are totally awful! Every person in the family has complained about the racks. The bowls and cups fall over. How is that even possible? I promise we have owned many other dishwashers. We are reasonably intelligent human beings. I, personally, have been successfully loading dishwashers for over 4 decades up until this one. We thought maybe we'd get used to putting the silverware on the third rack sideways. We did not. Instead our resentment grew each time a spoon flipped over and was full of water after the load. We are swapping out for the competitor's updated model. It costs, no joke, $1000 less. I loved it 1000% more. Even if it lasts 5 years again I'll make out ahead. I gave it 2 stars instead of 1 because 1) the dishes do get clean and 2) it is super quiet. Like, can't tell it's running quiet. The light is neat. It's not worth $1000. Obviously some people love the thing based on the fact it has 4.5 stars. Nobody in my home is part of that group.P.S. Another point is that the S brand allows you to operate each function separately, such as running just rinse without washing or just the baby storage function, whereas this model runs everything from washing to drying in one go. Sentence (English): Dishwasher works well.
Comments (English): [ Love it! ] || ---------------- || Dishwasher works well. I love all the options I can use to load dishes and I love that it automatically opens. Took me a minute to learn how to use it but once I got it it was good. Note it doesn't like being opened during a cycle and seemed like it took a sec to start back up. I believe if you open the door you have to press play before closing it again if you disrupt the cycle. Also if you don't have the right water connection home depot cannot install it. We ended up calling a plumber and they were able to install and haul away the old unit. In the end I kind of preferred this because they had to install a new hose and shut off switch that was compatible with the dishwasher. The unit ended up leaking at the piece the connects the hose to the unit. It took three plumbers in 2 days to realize they needed to tilt the machine so they could really turn the piece to tighten it fully. No more leaks after that. However I feel if home depot installed it and that happened it would have taken way more time to get someone out here to look at it. I am including a picture of the silver connector stop valve that you need or home depot cannot install it. If you don't have it then I would suggest paying for the install kit and hiring a plumber as the delivery guys cannot do this work and you will have to reschedule your delivery.

It took me a minute to learn how to use it, but once I did, it's been great. Good:. Quiet (though not super quiet). Washes dishes very well. Plenty of loading options. Auto-open feature is convenient. Bad / Notes:. Installation was a challenge. The dishwasher doesn't like being opened mid-cycle — if you do, you'll need to press “Play” before closing it again to resume. Home Depot cannot install it if you don't have the correct silver connector stop valve. If you're missing that valve, it's best to buy the install kit and hire a plumber instead. We had to call a plumber for installation; they replaced the hose and shut-off switch for proper compatibility. The unit initially leaked at the hose connection point — it took three plumbers over two days to figure out that the machine needed to be tilted slightly so the connector could be fully tightened. No more leaks after that fix. Honestly, I preferred using plumbers over Home Depot — if Home Depot had done it, getting someone back for a leak might've taken much longer. Tip:. Include or check for the silver connector stop valve before scheduling a Home Depot installation — without it, the delivery team can't complete the job and you'll have to reschedule. I am including a picture of the shut off valve that is needed.
